summary: Updates the new Telnet specification from RFC 495 to include modifications suggested since it was published. It also declares a moratorium on further changes, because the changeover from old to new Telnet was only a few months away.

eli5.summary: The remote-login rulebook got a last round of fixes. The authors then said no more changes for now, so everyone could switch over.

questions: what changed in the telnet specification in 1973
what is the telnet se command
why did rfc 562 declare a moratorium
subtitle: A last round of fixes to the new Telnet specification, followed by a freeze on further changes.

tldr.problem: Almost four months after the new Telnet specification was published, a few RFCs had suggested changes, and the switch from the old Telnet to the new one was only four months away.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 562 lists the changes folded into revised Telnet protocol and option specifications, which replace the earlier documents, and declares a moratorium on further suggestions until after the switchover.
tldr.outcome: It updates RFC 495. The moratorium covers changes to the specification, not new options.

today: RFC 562 updates RFC 495, and its status is listed as Unknown. It is a short change list, so read it together with the Telnet specifications it revises.

sections.title: Why the Specification Was Revised
sections.content:
The new Telnet Protocol specification had been out for almost four months. In that time only two RFCs had suggested modifications, and the most recent was distributed two months earlier. The date for moving from the old Telnet to the new Telnet, 1 January 1974, was only four months away.

The author therefore proposed to officially modify the specification to account for the suggestions. The RFC references RFCs 513 and 529 as the sources of most of the changes.
sections.eli5: Few people had asked for fixes, and the big switch date was getting close, so it was a good time to tidy up the rules.

sections.title: Changes to the Protocol Specification
sections.content:
The RFC lists changes by page of the earlier document. Most are clarifications:

  • The phrase "blocked on input" is removed.
  • An additional use of IP is mentioned.
  • The explanation of AO is expanded.
  • The definition of "print position" is clarified.
  • The description of the Telnet Synch Signal is reworked to match the ideas of RFC 529.
  • The explanation of the CR-NUL convention is expanded.

One change adds something new: a command called End of Subnegotiation Parameters (SE) is defined.
sections.eli5: Most fixes just explain confusing parts better. One adds a new signal that says "that is the end of the extra details".

sections.title: Changes to the Option Specifications
sections.content:
Two changes apply to the separate option specifications. The use of the SE command is explained, and doubling of IAC in subnegotiation parameters is now required.

The two attached documents replace the earlier Telnet Protocol Specification (NIC #15372) and Telnet Option Specifications (NIC #15373).
sections.eli5: The extra-details part of the rules got a clear ending signal, and one special symbol must be written twice so it is not mistaken for a command.

sections.title: The Moratorium
sections.content:
The RFC declares a moratorium on incorporating additional suggestions until after the switchover. The aim is a stable specification during the changeover.

The moratorium does not apply to options: no moratorium on the specification of additional options is required.
sections.eli5: Until the switch was done, no more rule changes were allowed. New add-on features could still be written.

references.text: RFC 513, referenced as a source of several changes.
RFC 529, referenced as a source of several changes.
